posts.title: Government updates belong in an open feed
posts.description: Government offices used to use their websites and mailing lists to publish their announcements. Now, the primary communication channel for most officials is a set of accounts spread across social media platforms. Senators post policy updates on Facebook. City representatives livestream their town halls on TikTok. The county office broadcasts emergencies on X. Mayoral offices are running Reels on I

posts.title: Go easy on the feeds, Reddit
posts.description: Update Right on cue, Reddit tucked its plan to haul its feeds to the curb into a bigger announcement about other changes. It'll stop supporting them on November 13, 2026. You can follow how we're tracking this in work item 161 . posts.title: YouTube, your feeds are broken
posts.description: In case you haven't caught on yet, some of us will just never be interested in being manipulated by those brain-rotting, never-ending homepage feeds you love shoving in our faces the moment we log in. We would rather use the feeds you offer for each of your channels. You know, the ones you're hiding?
